status: Validated single-program dispatch control; no production runtime change
reference: FastFlowLM src/lib/hrx/libllama_npu.so disassembly documented in amd2026-fastflow-review-2026-10-03.json

runtime.retrieval: FastFlowLM pinned fetch-hrx-release.sh verified archive and remote checksum; package in ignored build/hrx-release

protocol.dependency: Each output is the next input, ping-pong device-resident buffers
protocol.timed_scope: Host wall time for record/submit and waits; excludes initial upload, validation downloads, allocation, executable creation
protocol.order: XRT, HRX individual, HRX batch16; reversed on alternate trials
protocol.fixtures: constant, near-constant, two sinusoidal inputs; nonuniform gamma/beta; changed input every sample
protocol.buffer_guards: 256 bytes before and after each binding, identical XRT/HRX allocation sizes and offsets

reference_contract_note: An initial independently evolved 16-step FP64 trajectory exceeded 2e-4 on near-constant input (first reported error 0.000210). Replaced this ill-conditioned aggregate check with per-transition FP64 validation using actual FP32 inputs, at tighter 2e-5 tolerance, plus bitwise equality of every backend final output to the validated XRT trajectory. No kernel or production tolerance changed. Original failure log retained.
limitations: One resident norm program only; not a model speedup or a hardware-limit result.
No heterogeneous program transitions, large weights, recurrence state, or model prefill validated through HRX yet.
No proof of one hardware command per flush; HRX may submit multiple commands internally.
The small gain does not justify a production backend replacement by itself.
next: Measure alternating actual norm/projection programs and context reuse with this HRX API before deciding on runtime integration.
